Tutor Models:

| Judge | Link | Why use this judge |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Prometheus 2 7B | https://huggingface.co/prometheus-eval/prometheus-7b-v2.0 | Baseline we used for one pager; purpose-built for rubric grading |
| Atla Selene Mini 8B | https://huggingface.co/AtlaAI/Selene-1-Mini-Llama-3.1-8B | Supports binary and 1-5 rubric scoring with explanations |
| Flow-Judge | https://huggingface.co/flowaicom/Flow-Judge-v0.1 | Smaller, inexpensive judge |
| Claude Opus 4.8 | N/A | Strong general-purpose judge from a different model family; already available through truefoundry |
| GPT-5.5 | N/A | Strong frontier benchmark and already available |
| Gemini 3.6 Flash or Pro | N/A | Another independent family; Flash also tests the cost-efficient option |

* Frontier models may not be that great for cost, latency, and precision

**Validation Approach**

* Screen all judges on roughly 300-500 human-labeled response-criterion pairs  
* Use two trained human raters and adjudicate disagreements  
* Compare Macro-F1, critical-failure recall, human agreement, repeatability, robustness to harmless formatting/paraphrasing, parse failures, latency, and cost  
* Carry the best 2-3 judges onto a larger blind test, then select one primary judge and possibly one backup for ambiguous cases

Skills/Abilities:  
Example:  
Ability to explain the application of a math formula

Benchmark List:  
**TutorBench** (600 qs)  
**Pedagogy benchmark** (1,100 qs)  
**TutorEval** (\~800)

- Free response, seems to reference a textbook, STEM oriented

[MathTutorBench (MathDial)](https://github.com/eth-lre/mathtutorbench/blob/main/datasets/mathdial_bridge_hard.json)

- Could be interesting future work, since this has back-and-forth conversations, which is more reflective of an actual tutoring scenario

[MathQA](https://huggingface.co/datasets/allenai/math_qa)

- Has problem, rationale, annotated\_formula fields  
- Has options/correct answer fields as well (MCQ)  
- This could be a potential “tutoring” dataset → adjust the questions slightly so that the model is prompted to give explanation/tutoring assistance  
- We have annotated formula/rationale that could feed rubrics for LLM Judge

[MRBench](https://github.com/kaushal0494/UnifyingAITutorEvaluation/tree/main/BEA_Shared_Task_2025_Datasets): (\~1500)

- Maybe not too good since it doesn’t fit our Scenario / Rubric Schema very well.  
- For each prompt, it includes observed responses from different LLM models.  
- Also, built from Bridge \+ MathDial, possibly redundant if it doesn’t provide anything new.

[EEDI](https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/alejopaullier/eedi-external-dataset) (\~1800? Depends on how we format, maybe): 

- Can be used for misconception labeling (specific to “diagnosis” skill?)  
- MCQ, with “misconception” labeled for each wrong answer

[BRIDGE](https://huggingface.co/datasets/rose-e-wang/bridge) (700):

- Tutor conversations, instances where the student made a mistake \+ expert annotations about how to respond.  
- What the error was, how to respond, and why. Math-focused.

[EducationQ (MMLU-Pro-Stratified)](https://github.com/SunriserFuture/EducationQ/blob/main/src/data/dataset/mmlu-pro-stratified%2B/mmlu_pro_stratified_plus.json) (\~1300)

- MCQ questions covering many disciplines  
- Does not have explanations, but it is MCQ, so it shouldn’t matter  
- This github also generated teaching interactions between student agents and teaching agents in a conversational/multi-step approach. TODO \- evaluate results for this and see if this data can be used for evaluating multi-step tutoring examples

**EduBench** (9,600)  
[https://huggingface.co/datasets/DirectionAI/EduBench](https://huggingface.co/datasets/DirectionAI/EduBench)

- Non MCQ, 9 different teaching scenarios, and student interaction scenarios  
  - MCQ generation

**SQUAD 2.0:** [https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/thedevastator/squad2-0-a-challenge-for-question-answering-syst](https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/thedevastator/squad2-0-a-challenge-for-question-answering-syst)

- Reading comprehension FRQ; but answers are relatively short so it should be easy for an LLM judge to verify

**SVAMP**: [https://github.com/arkilpatel/SVAMP](https://github.com/arkilpatel/SVAMP)

- 1-2 step arithmetic word problems; open ended
